title: Field-extension invariance of the Picard group of a connected affine group over an algebraically closed field
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every field extension $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], put $G_K=G\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ and let $p_K:G_K\to G$ be its projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. For a scheme $Y$, write $\operatorname{Pic}(Y)$ for the abelian group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module], with tensor product as addition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and zero the class of $\mathcal O_Y$. Then pullback is an isomorphism of abelian groups $$p_K^*:\operatorname{Pic}(G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Pic}(G_K).$$ No algebraicity, separability, or perfection assumption is imposed on $K/k$; the trivial group is included.

source.place: WANTED locally: M. Brion, On Linearization of Line Bundles, J. Math. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 22 (2015), Lemma 2.3, printed pp.117–118, and Remark 2.2(v), printed p.117: specialize to algebraically closed k. The primary publisher PDF was read online; no Stacks tag located for this assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-reductive-affine-space-quotient] to $G/k$. Obtain $q:G\to H$ and $a:G\simeq H\times_k\mathbf A^n$ over $H$, where $H$ is reductive with a split maximal torus. Its scalar extension gives $G_K\simeq H_K\times_K\mathbf A^n$ over $H_K$. The same cited statement ensures that both $H$ and $H_K$ are smooth geometrically integral affine varieties over their respective fields.

Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-space-picard-invariance] to $H/k$ and $H_K/K$ and then the isomorphisms $a,a_K$. Thus $q^*$ and $q_K^*$ are isomorphisms on Picard groups. If $p_H:H_K\to H$, tensor pullback composition [def-pc-module-pullback] and $q\circ p_K=p_H\circ q_K$ give $p_K^*q^*=q_K^*p_H^*$. It remains to show that this particular pullback $p_H^*$ is bijective.

source.place: Brion Lemma 2.3, p.118, Pic(H_K) to Pic(G_K)

proof.text: Choose the split Borel pair $T\subseteq B\subseteq H$ supplied by [lem-sfb-split-reductive-characteristic-sequence], and put $Q=H/B$. The same node gives the two exact rows $X_k^*(T)\xrightarrow{c_k}\operatorname{Pic}(Q)\xrightarrow{f^*}\operatorname{Pic}(H)\to0$ and $X_K^*(T_K)\xrightarrow{c_K}\operatorname{Pic}(Q_K)\xrightarrow{f_K^*}\operatorname{Pic}(H_K)\to0$, with their scalar-extension vertical maps. Both squares commute, including $p_Q^*c_k(\chi)=c_K(\chi_K)$. This applies over arbitrary $K$, since the pair remains split.

source.place: Brion Lemma 2.3, p.118, equation (2); Milne Theorem 18.15

proof.text: Fix split coordinates $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$. Using the Hopf structure of $\mathbf G_m$ [def-sc-gm-ga] on each factor, a character over a field $F$ is a Laurent polynomial $u=\sum_m a_m t^m$ satisfying $\Delta(u)=u\otimes u$ and $\epsilon(u)=1$. Comparison of Laurent monomials gives $a_ma_l=0$ for $m\ne l$ and $a_m^2=a_m$, with $\sum_m a_m=1$. Since $F$ is a field, exactly one coefficient is $1$ and all others are zero. Thus all characters are uniquely $t^m$, $m\in\mathbf Z^r$, and scalar extension $X_k^*(T)\to X_K^*(T_K)$ is the identity on this exponent lattice. This argument also covers $r=0$.

source.place: Agent: elementary Laurent-coordinate verification of the split character lattice

proof.text: The pair of step 3 satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-split-flag-schubert-picard-lattice]: by [lem-sfb-split-reductive-characteristic-sequence], $B=U\rtimes T$ with $U$ split unipotent and $Q=H/B$ represented; the series of $U$ with $\mathbf G_a$ quotients, preceded by $B\supseteq U\rtimes T_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq U$ with $T_i=\mathbf G_m^{r-i}$ (normal since $T$ is commutative and $U$ normal), has quotients $\mathbf G_m$ or $\mathbf G_a$, so $B$ is split solvable. Apply [lem-sfb-split-flag-schubert-picard-lattice] to this split pair over $k$ and to $K/k$. Its geometrically integral boundary divisors give a basis of $\operatorname{Pic}(Q)$ and their scalar extensions give a basis of $\operatorname{Pic}(Q_K)$. The node states that $p_Q^*$ sends each basis class to the corresponding scalar-extended class. Hence $p_Q^*$ is an isomorphism: it is the identity on the integer coefficients of these bases.

source.place: Brion Lemma 2.3, p.118, flag Picard lattice and unchanged root datum

proof.text: Write $A,A_K$ for the character groups, $P,P_K$ for the flag Picard groups and $R,R_K$ for the group Picard groups of the two rows. The maps $u:A\to A_K$ and $v:P\to P_K$ are bijective by steps 4 and 5. Surjectivity: lift $y\in R_K$ to $z_K\in P_K$, write $z_K=v(z)$, and use the right square to obtain $y=p_H^*(f^*z)$. Injectivity: if $p_H^*(f^*z)=0$, exactness gives $v(z)=c_K(b_K)$; write $b_K=u(b)$. The left square yields $v(z)=v(c_k(b))$. Injectivity of $v$ gives $z=c_k(b)$, whence $f^*z=0$. Every element of $R$ is $f^*z$ by exactness. Therefore $p_H^*$ is bijective. Step 2 expresses $p_K^*=q_K^*p_H^*(q^*)^{-1}$, so the required pullback is an isomorphism of abelian groups. When $G=1$ every basis is empty and this same argument gives $0\simeq0$.

source.place: Agent: explicit cokernel diagram chase and the commuting pullback square
